exposure: 10-degree head-up tilt position during spinal anesthesia and operation
cohort: Participants were 44 parturient undergoing elective cesarean section, randomized to either a 10-degree head-up tilt or horizontal position during spinal anesthesia and the operation.
finding: The 10-degree head-up tilt position during spinal anesthesia for cesarean section significantly reduced the incidence of hypotension and ephedrine consumption, particularly before cord clamping, compared to the horizontal position.
mod_finding: The 10-degree head-up tilt position showed no adverse effects on newly-born babies.
